{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"20e964abc58526ee41ef0f23ebe0841429c199180d0cfa6c448f5ebb93b3288f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Required vehicle equipment, lights, tires and glass","heading":"C — Your vehicle: required equipment, brakes, bumpers and horn, headlights and restricted lights, mufflers and mirrors, seat belts and airbags, tires, windshields and tint, and fuel-saving habits","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Your vehicle: required equipment, brakes, bumpers and horn, headlights and restricted lights, mufflers and mirrors, seat belts and airbags, tires, windshields and tint, and fuel-saving habits
Knowledge domain: the equipment Minnesota requires on a vehicle before it may be driven on public roads, the headlight and lighting rules, which vehicles may use blue, flashing or strobe lights, tire pressure and tread limits, windshield and window tint limits, and habits that save fuel.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Before driving on public roads, make sure the vehicle is fully equipped and in good condition, read the owner's manual, and regularly check the lights, wipers, horn and tires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
When you get in, adjust your seat and mirrors, seat passengers where they do not block your view or interfere with driving, and buckle up and have every passenger do the same. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Every car and truck must have at least two separate brake systems, such as the foot brake and the parking or emergency brake. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Private passenger vehicles must have front and rear bumpers, while pickup trucks and vans need a front bumper plus either a rear bumper or reflectors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
A vehicle must have a working horn, and bells, sirens and whistles are reserved for emergency vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Use the horn to avoid a crash, never needlessly or to announce that you have arrived. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
The required-equipment diagram lists wipers, safety glass, a rearview mirror, horn, plates with a plate light, two ways to brake, high and low beam headlights, turn signals, bumpers, seat belts, a muffler, and a red taillight with red reflectors and a stop light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle except a motorcycle needs two white headlights that work on both high and low beam and red taillights that light up when the brake pedal is pressed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
High beams must light up objects on the road at least 350 feet ahead. [A02]
Why it matters: the high beam distance is a classic numeric item.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
Damaged headlights must be replaced, because a cracked lens lets in moisture and dust that cut light output and add glare for other drivers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
Dirty headlights can cut light output by as much as 75 percent, so clean them as often as the windshield. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
Have the headlights inspected at least once a year to make sure they are aimed correctly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
Daytime running lights may switch on automatically to make a vehicle more visible, but taillights and parking lights do not come on automatically. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
Headlights go on at sunset and stay on until sunrise, and also in rain, snow, hail, sleet or fog or whenever you cannot see the road at least 500 feet ahead. [A02]
Why it matters: the five hundred foot visibility rule is often confused with the high beam distance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
A white light must light the rear license plate so it can be seen at night, and every turn signal light on the vehicle must work. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
Blue lights are limited to snowplows, road maintenance equipment and authorized emergency vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
Flashing lights are limited to tow trucks, school buses, farm equipment, service vehicles, road maintenance equipment and authorized emergency vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
Strobe lamps are limited to school buses, snow removal equipment and rural mail carrier vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle needs a muffler to prevent sudden or prolonged loud noise such as popping or crackling, and the muffler should be checked regularly for carbon monoxide leaks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
Passenger vehicles need rearview mirrors, and a vehicle with no view through a rear window, such as a rental moving truck, or a pickup used for hauling needs an extra side mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
Minnesota requires seat belts in all vehicles and requires everyone to wear them, and belts should be kept clean and in good condition for all occupants. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
Airbags work together with seat belts but do not keep occupants from being thrown out, and a cluttered dashboard can turn objects into hazards when airbags inflate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
Look over your tires often for bulges, punctures, bald spots, cuts, cracks or uneven wear, and carry a good spare whose pressure you check often. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
Tires grip gravel or dirt roads less well than concrete or asphalt. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
A tire can lose up to 1 PSI of pressure a month, so check pressure often and never drive on under-inflated tires. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
The recommended tire pressure is on a sticker inside the driver's door or in the owner's manual, not the number printed on the tire sidewall. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
Check tire pressure before driving or at least three hours after driving, then add or release air until the gauge matches the recommended number. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
A tire is illegal when its tread is less than one-sixteenth of an inch deep. [A03]
Why it matters: the tread depth limit is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
In the penny test you place Lincoln's head into the shallowest tread groove, and if the tread covers any part of his head the tire is legal and safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A03
The view through the windshield and windows must not be blocked by cracks, discoloration, steam, frost, ice or snow, and nothing may hang between the driver and the windshield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A03
Stickers allowed by state law, such as park stickers, safety inspection stickers and toll devices, may go on the windshield, navigation units may mount near its bottom, and driver monitoring equipment may sit just behind, above or below the rearview mirror. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A03
A windshield may not be made of, covered with or treated with any material that makes it more reflective or lets less light through. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A03
Side or rear window tint applied after Aug. 1, 1985 must be labeled with the percentage of light it transmits and reflects. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A03
Tint that transmits less than 50 percent or reflects more than 20 percent of light is allowed only on a pickup's rear window or on the rear and side windows of a van, limousine or funeral home vehicle. [A03]
Why it matters: the fifty and twenty percent tint limits are easy to swap.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A03
A vehicle with a glass windshield must have working wipers, and defrosters are needed to keep the windshield and windows free of steam and frost. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A03
Passenger vehicles need fenders or other wheel guards so the tires do not throw water, dirt and debris into the air. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A04
Save fuel by keeping the engine tuned, the tires properly inflated and the recommended grade of motor oil in the engine. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A04
Drive efficiently by combining errands, avoiding speeding, hard acceleration and sudden braking, obeying the speed limit, removing heavy items you do not need, and using cruise control and overdrive on the highway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A04
Public transportation, carpools, ridesharing, biking or walking are recommended whenever possible to save fuel. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

Misconceptions: the correct tire pressure comes from the door sticker, not the tire sidewall; daytime running lights do not turn on taillights; airbags do not replace seat belts and cannot prevent ejection; blue lights are not allowed on ordinary tow trucks, which may use flashing lights only.
Mnemonics: high beams reach three hundred fifty feet, headlights on when you cannot see five hundred feet; tint below fifty or above twenty is for the back of trucks and vans; Lincoln's head hidden means the tread is good.
Glossary: PSI means pounds per square inch, the unit of tire pressure; tread means the grooved rubber that grips the road; daytime running lights mean lights that switch on automatically in daylight; wheel guards mean fenders that stop tires from throwing debris.
